summary: Prioritize short, highly punchy hook sentences under 10 words to maximize initial viewer retention. Focus on visceral, counter-intuitive bodily reactions like eating and biological defense mechanisms. Use dramatic, short-form titles instead of descriptive academic summaries to drive algorithmic interest. Eliminate lengthy, explanatory hook clauses that reveal the full context too early. Keep average view durations high by maintaining active curiosity gaps in the middle segments of the video.
winning_hooks: Fresh pineapple is literally eating you back.
Your eyes are leaking right now, and your brain is hiding it.
This shark is older than the United States.
avoid: Starting hooks with explanatory phrases like 'Garlic usually doesn't make you cry when you chop it, because...'
Using long, academic titles that lack curiosity-driven contrast or emotional hooks.
next_experiment: Test an A/B split on a new biological topic comparing a 6-word shocking hook ('Your saliva is currently dissolving you') against a standard descriptive hook ('Why your mouth produces liquid all day') while tracking averageViewPercentage for rewatch value.
